precepts.text: Jacob fled into the country of Syria, and Israel served for a wife, and for a wife he kept sheep.
precepts.point: The father is Jacob: Jacob fled into the country of Syria, and Israel served for a wife, and for a wife he kept sheep, as we read in Genesis.

note.label: Deuteronomy 26: The Firstfruits Confession and a Peculiar People

precepts.why:
“A Syrian ready to perish was my father, and he went down into Egypt, and sojourned there with a few”. Who is the father? Jacob. Hosea says: “And Jacob fled into the country of Syria, and Israel served for a wife, and for a wife he kept sheep.”

Jacob, who is Israel, fled into the country of Syria and served there for a wife, keeping sheep, as we read in Genesis. That is the Syrian ready to perish of the firstfruits confession, the father who went down into Egypt with a few and became there a nation, great, mighty, and populous.

precepts.text: A new king which knew not Joseph set taskmasters over Israel to afflict them with their burdens, and they built for Pharaoh treasure cities.
precepts.point: There arose up a new king over Egypt which knew not Joseph; fearing that the children of Israel were more and mightier than they, Egypt set over them taskmasters to afflict them with their burdens, and they built for Pharaoh the treasure cities, Pithom and Raamses.

note.label: Deuteronomy 26: The Firstfruits Confession and a Peculiar People

precepts.why:
“And the Egyptians evil entreated us, and afflicted us, and laid upon us hard bondage”. Exodus tells how it began: “Now there arose up a new king over Egypt, which knew not Joseph. And he said unto his people, Behold, the people of the children of Israel are more and mightier than we: Come on, let us deal wisely with them; lest they multiply, and it come to pass, that, when there falleth out any war, they join also unto our enemies, and fight against us, and so get them up out of the land.”

Fearing that the children of Israel were more and mightier than they, Egypt dealt with them: “Therefore they did set over them taskmasters to afflict them with their burdens. And they built for Pharaoh treasure cities, Pithom and Raamses.” The taskmasters and the burdens are the affliction, and building Pithom and Raamses for Pharaoh is the hard bondage the confession speaks of.

precepts.text: The Lord hath chosen Jacob unto himself, and Israel for his peculiar treasure.
precepts.point: Which in time past were not a people, but are now the people of God: we were called by other names, African American, Dominican, Negro, but now we are coming into the understanding that we are actually the children of Israel.

note.label: Deuteronomy 26: The Firstfruits Confession and a Peculiar People

precepts.why:
“And the Lord hath avouched thee this day to be his peculiar people, as he hath promised thee”. The psalm says the same: “For the Lord hath chosen Jacob unto himself, and Israel for his peculiar treasure.”

The peculiar people avouched here is Jacob, Israel, chosen unto himself for his peculiar treasure.

precepts.text: A chosen generation, a royal priesthood, a peculiar people, which in time past were not a people, but are now the people of God.
precepts.point: Which in time past were not a people, but are now the people of God: we were called by other names, African American, Dominican, Negro, but now we are coming into the understanding that we are actually the children of Israel.

note.label: Deuteronomy 26: The Firstfruits Confession and a Peculiar People

precepts.why:
Peter writes to that peculiar people: “But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people; that ye should shew forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light”. The peculiar people the Lord avouched here is the peculiar people Peter writes to. We were called out of our sins into the light, and the light is the commandments and the law.

“Which in time past were not a people, but are now the people of God: which had not obtained mercy, but now have obtained mercy.” We were called by other names, African American, Dominican, Negro; but now we are coming into the understanding that we are actually the children of Israel, the people of God.

precepts.text: The commandment is a lamp, and the law is light: the marvellous light we were called into.
precepts.point: Which in time past were not a people, but are now the people of God: we were called by other names, African American, Dominican, Negro, but now we are coming into the understanding that we are actually the children of Israel.

note.label: Deuteronomy 26: The Firstfruits Confession and a Peculiar People

precepts.why:
Peter says we were called out of darkness into his marvellous light. What is that light? “For the commandment is a lamp; and the law is light; and reproofs of instruction are the way of life”.

The commandment is a lamp and the law is light: the marvellous light we were called into is the commandments and the law. We were called out of our sins into the light, and that is why the Lord avouched his peculiar people “that thou shouldest keep all his commandments”.

precepts.text: If ye will obey my voice and keep my covenant, ye shall be a peculiar treasure unto me above all people.
precepts.point: Which in time past were not a people, but are now the people of God: we were called by other names, African American, Dominican, Negro, but now we are coming into the understanding that we are actually the children of Israel.

note.label: Deuteronomy 26: The Firstfruits Confession and a Peculiar People

precepts.why:
The Lord avouched Israel his peculiar people “as he hath promised thee”, and here is the promise: “Now therefore, if ye will obey my voice indeed, and keep my covenant, then ye shall be a peculiar treasure unto me above all people: for all the earth is mine: And ye shall be unto me a kingdom of priests, and an holy nation. These are the words which thou shalt speak unto the children of Israel.”

A peculiar treasure, a kingdom of priests, an holy nation: the same words Peter uses, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people. And the condition is the same in both places: obey my voice and keep my covenant, keep all his commandments. These are the words spoken unto the children of Israel.

precepts.text: Thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God, chosen to be a special people unto himself, above all people upon the face of the earth.
precepts.point: This is the same word given earlier in Deuteronomy, among other scriptures: thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God, chosen to be a special people unto himself, above all people that are upon the face of the earth.

note.label: Deuteronomy 26: The Firstfruits Confession and a Peculiar People

precepts.why:
“that thou mayest be an holy people unto the Lord thy God, as he hath spoken.” Where had he spoken it? Earlier in Deuteronomy, among other scriptures: “For thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God: the Lord thy God hath chosen thee to be a special people unto himself, above all people that are upon the face of the earth.”

It is the same word: an holy people unto the Lord thy God, chosen above all people that are upon the face of the earth, made high above all nations which he hath made, in praise, and in name, and in honour. As he had spoken it in chapter 7, so he avouched it here.
